ctx.en: It has come to light that the company turned a blind eye to wrongdoing at the factory for years.

bad.s: 彼女[かのじょ]の素晴[すば]らしい演技[えんぎ]に、思[おも]わず{目[め]をつぶった}。
bad.en: (meant: I was dazzled by her wonderful performance)
bad.why: You overlook flaws, not something you admire. For being struck by it say me o ubawareta or mitoreta.

bad.s: 今日[きょう]中[じゅう]にこの問題[もんだい]に{目[め]をつぶって}、必[かなら]ず解決[かいけつ]します。
bad.en: (meant: I'll concentrate on this problem today and solve it)
bad.why: It means deliberately not looking at something, the opposite of focusing on it. Say shuuchuu suru or torikumu.

mean: to be unable to believe one's eyes

use.how: Predicate, usually past, for something seen that seems impossible: 結果を見て目を疑った. Also 目を疑うほど〜, and the stronger 我が目を疑う.

near.diff: 耳を疑う is for something heard; 目を疑う is for something seen.
目を丸くする is the surprised face others can see; 目を疑う is the inner disbelief at what you are seeing.

cue: You check the scoreboard: your team, which has lost all season, is ahead by forty points. You blink and look again.

ctx.s: テストの点数[てんすう]を見[み]て、{目[め]を疑[うたが]った}。
ctx.en: When I saw my test score, I couldn't believe my eyes.

ctx.s: 四月[しがつ]なのに外[そと]が一面[いちめん]の雪[ゆき]で、{目[め]を疑[うたが]った}。
ctx.en: It was April, yet everything outside was covered in snow. I couldn't believe my eyes.

ctx.s: 「見[み]て、この請求書[せいきゅうしょ]。」「え、ゼロが一[ひと]つ多[おお]くない？{目[め]を疑[うたが]った}よ。」
ctx.en: "Look at this bill." "What, isn't there an extra zero? I couldn't believe my eyes."

ctx.s: 久[ひさ]しぶりに帰[かえ]った故郷[こきょう]の駅前[えきまえ]は、{目[め]を疑[うたが]う}ほど変[か]わっていた。
ctx.en: The area by the station in my hometown, which I hadn't visited in years, had changed beyond belief.

ctx.s: ニュースで流[なが]れた被害[ひがい]の映像[えいぞう]に、多[おお]くの人[ひと]が{目[め]を疑[うたが]った}。
ctx.en: Many people could not believe their eyes at the footage of the damage on the news.

ctx.s: 掲示板[けいじばん]に自分[じぶん]の番号[ばんごう]を見[み]つけたとき、私[わたし]は思[おも]わず{我[わ]が目[め]を疑[うたが]った}。
ctx.en: When I found my number on the board, I honestly couldn't believe my own eyes.

bad.s: 電話[でんわ]で合格[ごうかく]したと聞[き]いて、{目[め]を疑[うたが]った}。
bad.en: (meant: when I heard on the phone that I'd passed, I couldn't believe it)
bad.why: Something heard calls for mimi o utagau; me o utagau is only for what you see.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]の話[はなし]は嘘[うそ]だと思[おも]うので、{目[め]を疑[うたが]う}。
bad.en: (meant: I think his story is a lie, so I don't trust him)
bad.why: It is stunned disbelief at something you see, not suspicion of a person. Say kare o utagau or shin'you dekinai.
